mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 4% over the prior month reduces the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows, lowering the present value of expected dividends and earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by 0.25% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or flat when FEDFUNDS rises by 0.25% in the prior month, with p-value > 0.05 in a two-tailed test.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which raises consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 10,000 in one month while UNRATE falls by > 0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: No statistically significant positive return in the 60-day window when both PAYEMS up >10k and UNRATE down >0.2pp (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in retail sales (HOUST) above 2% for three consecutive months indicates accelerating consumer demand, which lowers expected discount rates and boosts equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite monthly HOUST growth > 2% for three months (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 5% in a month suggests supply-side shocks that reduce future supply capacity, raising risk premia and depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 5% in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO contracts by >5% (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2.5% for two consecutive months, the market anticipates tighter policy, causing a sharp rise in the risk-free rate and a decline in equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by > 0.5% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or flat during such inflation episodes (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% triggers a labor market tightening that reduces wage growth expectations and increases the cost of capital, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% in one month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE falls below 4% (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail employment (HOUST) and a simultaneous decline in consumer confidence (not available in evidence - so skip this proxy) cannot be used; instead, use a proxy like GDPC1 for GDP momentum. Instead: A 3-month acceleration in GDP (GDPC1) growth above 2% suggests robust demand, lowering discount rates and supporting positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite GDPC1 growing >2% for 3 months (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising while UNRATE steady), the S&P 500 anticipates higher future interest rates, which increases the cost of capital and compresses equity valuations, producing negative forward returns over the next 20 days regardless of other signals.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS is rising and UNRATE is flat (p-value > 0.05).
